title: LLM4OM documentation
description: From your first optimization problem to methods, solvers and deployment.
text: LLM4OM turns natural-language problems and data into optimization models and calls solvers to compute plans. Describe requirements, inspect decisions and the modeling process, then revise conditions, compare alternatives and export results. Choose an entry point Entry Starting point Next actions Optimization chat Send a problem or idea Clarify, compute, query, revise and compare scenarios Manual modeling A prepared statement and data Edit inputs, choose settings and follow execution Requirements assistant A developing business idea Create an editable statement and attachments First-time users can complete the production quickstart. To run a service, see installation. From requirements to a usable plan Workflow overviewDownload SVG A run retains statement, attachments, configuration, formulation, code, values and steps. Original and revised plans remain connected to their inputs. Everyday features Task Guide Add tables and edit fields or values Upload and edit data Read production, staffing or allocation decisions Results and exports Query a decision or total costs Discuss a plan Change a requirement and compute another plan Revisions Compare budgets, demand or resources Scenarios Find past tasks and record decisions History, tags and reports Understand modeling and computation Methods covers 13 workflows with mechanisms, Mermaid diagrams, step-by-step examples and current parameters: generation, feedback repair, layered validation, type retrieval, component search and data binding. Libraries and solvers covers nine libraries, native interfaces, backends and complete code. Production, staffing, assignment, convex quadratic and nonlinear examples help select a computation path. Watch and interact Docs include localized workbench recordings, screenshots and interactive examples. Download quickstart data, step through method artifacts, or change solver-example parameters and inspect computed results. The interface supports Chinese, English and light/dark/system themes. Desktop dividers resize work areas; narrow screens use tabs for main content and assistants. Teams and scripts Team deployment covers shared services, HTTPS and access configuration. Usage and backups covers quotas, concurrency and data maintenance. CLI and Python runs the same modeling workflows from existing programs. LLM4OM is developed by the EIPI team, with publicly maintained source and documentation.

title: Your first plan
description: Build, solve and revise a small production plan.
text: Complete a production task from description through modeling, solving, export and revision. The example includes a statement, downloadable data and localized workbench recordings. 1. Prepare a service and preset Open your team service or install one. Choose an available LLM preset; see preset setup to add one. Send the problem in Optimization chat or use manual modeling. This example uses Direct, Pyomo and AUTO to match the recording. 2. Enter the problem Produce nonnegative integer quantities of products A and B. A earns CNY 3 and uses 2 cutting hours and 1 finishing hour per unit. B earns CNY 2 and uses 1 cutting hour and 2 finishing hours per unit. There are 8 hours of each resource. Calculate the production plan with maximum total profit. Start modeling and follow formulation, code and solving. title: Install and launch
description: Start the platform with Docker Compose or a local Python environment.
text: If you already have a team service address, open it in a browser. To run your own service, Docker Compose installs the workbench, server and solver environment. Prepare an environment Setup Requirements Use Docker Compose Docker, Compose v2.24+, model-service configuration Personal or team service Python service Python 3.11–3.13, uv, Docker, model-service configuration Development or existing Python setup Data lives in a workspace or Compose volume. Choose a machine with persistent storage and access to the model service. Start with Docker Compose git clone https://github.com/Fangziyang0910/LLM4OM.git cd LLM4OM cp .env.example .env chmod 600 .env Edit .env with provider, endpoint, model ID and key; see LLM presets. Then run: docker compose up -d --build docker compose ps After building, open http://localhost:8767. Initial setup downloads dependencies and builds the Worker. Inspect startup with docker compose logs -f app. Confirm setup in the workbench Check the default preset and backend options. Complete the production quickstart; the run should retain quantities, formulation, code and stages. Then add attachments or try Optimization chat. Other devices can use the server address. See team deployment for shared access and HTTPS. Start from Python In the cloned repository: uv sync --all-extras uv run llm4om build-worker uv run llm4om serve --workspace runs/web --port 8767 This uses bundled workbench build files and Docker solver sandboxes. runs/web retains history and presets; use --workspace for another location. Maintenance commands Action Command Status docker compose ps Logs docker compose logs -f app Update git pull, then docker compose up -d --build Apply environment changes docker compose up -d app Stop, retaining data volume docker compose down See presets for connections, backends for solver setup and backups for persistent data. Website and platform addresses GitHub Pages serves the website and Docs. The complete platform runs Python and solver services on the configured machine. Team members calculate through that deployed service address.

title: How modeling works
description: Understand methods, LLMs, modeling libraries, solvers and saved runs.
text: LLM4OM connects requirements, modeling, computation and plan management. These terms map to settings and artifacts in the workbench. Run data flow Workflow overviewDownload SVG Attachments map file names to complete text. build_model(data) parses inputs and returns a native model. The platform executes and retains results. Four configuration objects Term Role Example Method Generation, checking and repair orchestration Direct, TriVAL, BIND LLM preset Service and request configuration Team endpoint and model ID Library Variables, objective and constraints Pyomo, CPMpy, CVXPY Backend Mathematical computation HiGHS, CP-SAT, Gurobi, Ipopt One configuration might be “Feedback Repair + team preset + Pyomo + HiGHS.” Run information retains selections and the actual engine. Four types of model information Information Meaning Production example Parameters Known input values Unit profit and capacity Variables Quantities or choices to determine A and B quantities Objective Expression to minimize or maximize Total profit Constraints Relationships decisions must satisfy Hours and minimum orders Indices extend these objects across products, dates, employees and nodes. Units connect statements, data and result labels. Runs and plans A run contains inputs, settings, steps, formulation, code and execution. A plan is its computed decision result. Revisions create new runs; scenarios connect runs to one baseline. The conversation's current plan determines the basis for questions and changes. Common statuses Status Meaning optimal Optimal result for the current model feasible A feasible plan is available locally_optimal Local result from a native nonlinear path infeasible Current requirements cannot hold together unbounded Objective is unbounded along a feasible direction time_limit Limit reached; inspect retained solution and feedback Execution or validation failure Read the specific stage and feedback Status, values and method validation remain in the run. See results for daily use and methods or solvers for mechanisms and interfaces.

title: Clarify requirements
description: Turn an initial idea into an editable problem statement and data.
text: “Clarify requirements through conversation” develops an initial idea into an editable problem statement and attachments. Use it when the task is known but goals, rules or data need further discussion. Start from a draft or a blank page Existing homepage text and attachments carry into the conversation. You can also start with “Schedule next week's employees across three stores.” The assistant updates the draft and asks for information affecting the next step. Desktop keeps the problem and data beside the assistant. Narrow screens use tabs. Edit the draft directly or switch to Markdown preview. How a draft develops Workflow overviewDownload SVG FOLLOW THE EXAMPLE←Play→ 1. Describe the task2. Add key rules3. Edit the draft4. Hand off1. Describe the taskState the objects, time horizon and goal. The assistant organizes the available information. Schedule next week's employees across three stores and control total staffing cost. 2. Add key rulesTurn answers into concrete requirements and list the data still needed. At least 3 people per store per day; at most 5 days per person; weekend supervisor. Data: costs, availability and supervisor qualifications. 3. Edit the draftEdit rules, units or wording directly, save, then continue discussing. Allow movement between stores; one store per employee per day. Columns: employee, date, availability, daily cost, supervisor. 4. Hand offChoose settings and start modeling. The method receives the current statement and attachments. Handoff: complete draft + current attachments The run saves this input version. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. A reusable problem structure Task: objects to arrange and time horizon. Decisions: quantities, selections or sequences to determine. Objective: minimum cost, maximum profit or another explicit goal. Rules: individual requirements. Data: file names, field meanings, units and index mappings. Start with the parts you know. Keep costs, times and quantities in explicit units; edit attachment headers to make them clear. Save, search and hand off Leaving the editor saves manual edits; “Save draft” is also available. Sending a message or starting modeling saves pending changes first. Attachments are saved after reading. Search shows queries and sources. Adopt useful business rules into the draft. “Use for modeling” returns the draft to the workbench; settings and modeling are also available directly in the current workspace. Continue working Conversation history retains requirement development; runs retain the handoff statement and data. Unsent text stays in the current browser tab and survives refresh. Stop or retry a turn, then continue refining. Next see data editing and run settings. For clarification and computation in one continuing conversation, use Chat Agent.

title: Configure a run
description: Select a method, modeling library, solver backend and LLM preset.
text: Run settings select the modeling workflow, code library, computation engine and LLM. The homepage shows a configuration summary; open “View run settings” or “Adjust settings” for all options. Configure one run Workflow overviewDownload SVG For production/transport LP/MILP, start with compatible Pyomo or PuLP backends. title: Understand infeasibility
description: Use solver evidence to inspect requirements that cannot hold together.
text: An infeasible result means the current requirements cannot hold together in the submitted model. When specific solver evidence is available, the platform connects conflicting constraints to business rules and provides a revision action. A concrete conflict Add B≥5 to production with 8 finishing hours. The relevant expressions are B≥5, A+2B≤8 and nonnegative quantities. The explanation maps these to minimum orders and finishing capacity. title: Choose a modeling method
description: Compare the workflows, scope and configuration of 13 methods.
text: A modeling method controls how the LLM builds formulations and code, and when it checks, retries or compares candidates. The generated model then goes to a solver, which computes decision values and the objective. Choose by the difficulty you face Main difficulty Start with Inspect Need a quick first model Direct Domains, constraints and data binding Executable code may miss rules Feedback Repair Specific review after solving Need to separate interpretation, formulation and code errors TriVAL Layered checks and attribution Many rules need component inspection OptiMUS 0.3 Constraint-to-formula-to-code mapping Want to inspect role collaboration Chain-of-Experts Useful information added by later experts Want problem-type templates OptiTree Match path and template applicability Want formulation before code and rechecks OR-LLM-Agent Rounds and actually executed code versions Need a retained modeling explanation ORThought Reasons for concrete modeling choices Want five-element formulation and correction LLMOPT Formulation errors versus code errors Want candidate-model search AutoFormulation Pruning, rewards and final ranking Need constraint-level meaning checks SAC-Opt Blind backtranslation and selective repair Large JSON/CSV cannot fit conveniently in prompts BIND Schema and full-data execution binding Want public type hints and continuing feedback OptiMind Public hint scope and checks after success Each article expands the mechanism, example and current parameters. Four checks answer different questions Workflow overviewDownload SVG Semantic checks interpret “each employee works at most five days.” Formulation checks require a sum for each employee. Code checks inspect indices and domains. The solver determines feasibility and optimality for the submitted model. Repair loops also differ. Some read only execution errors, others review the problem, and others backtranslate individual constraints. Compare what triggers each check and which stage receives its feedback. Read different workflows on one example For the production problem, Direct generates formulation and code before solving. Feedback Repair adds a review after solving. TriVAL creates semantic, formulation and code validation artifacts. Open the worked examples to follow the same rule through those stages. Quickstart provides the statement, data and recording. Method comparison provides side-by-side runs. What determines call cost Direct uses one modeling call. Feedback Repair without repairs uses two calls and one solve. Component methods scale with rule count; validation methods scale with failed checks and returns. AutoFormulation's candidate sampling has a substantially larger default budget. Elapsed time depends on provider latency, attachment size, output length and solving difficulty. The platform records actual calls, usage and elapsed time; parameter tables come from current presets. Problem scope and combinations OptiMUS, CoE, OptiTree, OR-LLM-Agent, AutoFormulation and SAC-Opt currently target LP/MILP. Other methods run according to the chosen model, library and backend. All nine libraries can be selected, but actual mathematics must fit the library and backend. For example, CPMpy expresses finite-domain decisions, OSQP handles continuous convex quadratic programs, and Ipopt seeks local solutions for smooth nonlinear models. Use solver selection to match these structures. Make comparisons informative Fix the problem, attachments, LLM preset, library, backend and limits, then vary one factor. Record rule coverage, domains, actual solutions, solver status, validation status, call count and solve count. Use differences and failed stages to decide whether to clarify requirements, improve data descriptions or change the checking workflow. See method and LLM comparison for the UI workflow.

title: Direct
description: Generate the mathematical model and solver code in one LLM call.
text: Direct sends the problem, data description and modeling-library contract to the LLM in one request. The reply contains a formulation and complete code. The platform executes the code and calls a real solver. This short workflow is useful for a first attempt and as a baseline for other methods. What the method does Direct translates the description into variables, an objective and constraints, then writes the corresponding model code. One reply contains both outputs. The platform executes that code and solves the model. Consider two products. A and B earn 3 and 2 per unit. They use 2 and 1 cutting hours, and 1 and 2 finishing hours. Each resource has 8 hours available. title: Feedback Repair
description: Review the solved model against the problem and repair specific errors.
text: Feedback Repair adds execution, review against the original problem and targeted repair to Direct. It addresses a common failure: code runs and the solver reports optimality, but a business rule was translated incorrectly. Why review after a successful solve Suppose production requires at least 3 units of B, but the code says B <= 3. The solver can return (3, 2) with objective 13. This is correct for the wrong model and violates the requirement. Fixing Python exceptions cannot detect it. The reviewer reads the problem, formulation, code, execution feedback and available conflict evidence. It checks coefficients, domains, constraint directions and data binding, then accepts or identifies a repair. Workflow and worked example Workflow overview · Choose an example stage to inspect its inputs and outputs.Download SVGFOLLOW THE EXAMPLE←Play→ 1. First model2. Review3. Repair and solve4. Accept or report1. First modelAssume generation reverses the demand constraint. The solver does not read the business description and can still report optimality. Required: B ≥ 3 Hypothetical error: B ≤ 3 Wrong-model optimum: A = 3, B = 2, objective 13 2. ReviewName the mismatch. The mismatch becomes specific repair feedback. Decision: repair Reason: a minimum became an upper bound; B = 2 violates B ≥ 3. 3. Repair and solveRestore B ≥ 3, preserve the other requirements and execute the revised code. 2A + B ≤ 8; A + 2B ≤ 8; B ≥ 3 Integer optimum: A = 2, B = 3, objective 12 4. Accept or reportThe lower objective is the cost of satisfying the requirement. Accept after review, or retain artifacts and report an unresolved error when the budget ends. Original objective: 13. With B ≥ 3: 12. Both models and results remain available. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. What should be repaired Feedback Appropriate response Syntax error or invalid return object Repair from execution feedback Whole products modeled as continuous Restore integers and solve again Genuine demand and resource conflict Retain reviewed infeasibility and original requirements Time limit with a feasible incumbent Save status and available incumbent No objective for a satisfaction problem Check whether finding a satisfying assignment was intended Budget and final artifacts At most three repairs are shared across format, execution and modeling errors. A run without repair uses two LLM calls and one solve. Later explanations can add calls. An incomplete later reply preserves the last formulation, code and result actually executed. A failed or unparseable review also preserves computation and records the failure. Using and reading the method Select Feedback Repair in run settings. Inspect the initial model, review reason and changed expressions. Follow each repair reason to its rule and code expression. Use it for a short workflow with review after execution. For layered validation, see TriVAL. For constraint backtranslation and frozen accepted components, see SAC-Opt. Implementation source This project maintains the method and its shared Direct generator. The review node and repair loop are published alongside the generator. title: TriVAL
description: Validate semantics, formulation and code, with revisions across stages.
text: TriVAL separates three questions: was the problem understood correctly, does the formulation express that understanding, and does the code implement the formulation? Each level has construction, validation and revision. A code-stage finding can send the workflow back to the formulation. What each level checks Level Artifacts Example failure Revision Semantics Facts, ambiguities and resolutions Interpreting coverage per shift as a daily total Extract facts again or revise ambiguity resolutions Formulation Parameters, indices, variables, objective and constraints Missing per-shift coverage or reversing a minimum Revise locally or rebuild the formulation Code Native model code and execution evidence Wrong indices, domains or implementation Repair code, or return to the formulation if that is the cause Each validation result identifies the stage to revise: extracted facts, mathematical expressions or their implementation. Workflow and worked example Workflow overview · Choose an example stage to inspect its inputs and outputs.Download SVGFOLLOW THE EXAMPLE←Play→ 1. Semantic facts2. Formulation3. Execute and attribute4. Report separately1. Semantic factsSeparate profits, processing times, resource limits and whole-unit requirements. An additional requirement of at least 3 units of B must remain a demand fact. Facts: whole products; 8 hours of each resource; B at least 3. Check interpretation: unit net profit and processing hours per unit. 2. FormulationParameter/index, variable, objective and constraint experts construct in parallel. A selector assembles the formulation, which is checked against the facts. max 3A + 2B 2A + B ≤ 8; A + 2B ≤ 8; B ≥ 3 A, B are nonnegative integers 3. Execute and attributeIf code omits B ≥ 3 but the formulation includes it, repair code. If the formulation also omits it, return to that level. Implementation omission → repair build_model(data) Formulation omission → revise formulation, then regenerate code The routes address different causes. 4. Report separatelyThe correct integer optimum is 12. The final record shows numerical results and each stage's validation status. Solver evidence: A = 2, B = 3, objective 12 Record semantic / formulation / code validation separately Stage feedback records the final validation decision. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. How validation failures are routed Semantic checks distinguish faithful facts, relevant ambiguities and consistent resolutions. Faulty facts or ambiguity identification cause extraction again; inconsistent resolutions return to ambiguity resolution. Formulation checks can request partial revision or a new construction by the experts. Code is executed before code validation. Attribution to the formulation sends the outer workflow back to that level. An upstream stage can proceed with its latest artifacts after reaching its limit. The platform reports each unpassed stage at exit. Reading a run effectively Choose a rule that is easy to misinterpret and follow it through facts, formulation and code. For “each employee works at most five days,” check for an employee index with a separate constraint for each employee. Then inspect whether later artifacts actually address the validator's finding. The run retains solver values and stage validation feedback. Comparisons can inspect status, failed stages, revisions and actual call usage. Requirements and budget Select TriVAL and a library/backend supporting the intended mathematics. Each stage allows at most five validations; code execution allows twenty attempts. Total LLM use depends on nodes and return paths. For DeepSeek, forced tool choice requires thinking mode to be disabled in the preset: {"thinking":{"type":"disabled"}}. See LLM presets. Related methods and implementation Feedback Repair reviews the model after solving; TriVAL moves checks into separate levels. SAC-Opt focuses on the consistency of backtranslated constraint code. The platform ports the pinned SCUT-EIPI/TriVAL implementation, retaining its graph, nodes, prompts and loops. It supplies the LLM and sandbox, maps input and reports unresolved validation at exit. title: OptiMUS 0.3
description: Extract parameters, objectives and constraints, then assemble component code.
text: OptiMUS 0.3 constructs a model component by component. It extracts parameters, objectives and constraints, formulates and codes individual components, then assembles and executes them. Intermediate artifacts make a long generation task easier to inspect. From rules to components “Only 8 cutting hours” is a business rule; 2A+B≤8 is its formulation; a native Constraint is its implementation. OptiMUS keeps these stages visible so readers can follow changes in meaning. Objectives and constraints are handled separately. Constraints receive redundancy and confidence checks. A low-confidence item can be retained, removed or modified. These are LLM judgments: check whether removal eliminates a duplicate or loses a distinct requirement. Workflow and worked example Workflow overview · Choose an example stage to inspect its inputs and outputs.Download SVGFOLLOW THE EXAMPLE←Play→ 1. Parameters and rules2. Check components3. Assemble code4. Execute and debug1. Parameters and rulesIdentify profit, resource consumption and capacities as parameters. Keep the cutting and finishing coefficients in separate resource rows. Profit: A=3, B=2 C1: cutting capacity 8, consumption (2,1) C2: finishing capacity 8, consumption (1,2) 2. Check componentsRepeated wording can be removed. Cutting and finishing have different coefficients and remain separate constraints. C1 → 2A + B ≤ 8 C2 → A + 2B ≤ 8 Preserve nonnegative integer domains. 3. Assemble codeComponents enter one build_model(data). Names, indices and parameters must agree across components. setup + variables + C1 + C2 + objective + return model Generated code builds; the platform solves. 4. Execute and debugThe correct model gives A=3, B=2 and objective 13. If debugging occurs, check that changes preserve component meaning. At most 3 execution/debug attempts Infeasible or unbounded statuses can also trigger debugging. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. Parameter data and confidence An attached params.json in the upstream format supplies parameters directly. Otherwise the method extracts them, including values, from the problem. The parameter artifact retains each name, shape, meaning and value. Constraint confidence uses five-point judgments with bounded retries. Low-confidence items receive further feedback deciding retention, removal or revision. The process retains those decisions and the updated list. How its repair differs Execution debugging treats optimality as success and also preserves explicitly local optimality from compatible backends. Infeasible and unbounded models can therefore enter debugging. Feedback Repair instead permits a reviewed, genuinely infeasible model to end normally. When infeasibility is plausible, check whether debugging changes a hard requirement. For checking code against individual constraint meanings, see SAC-Opt. Scope and reading a run The current method targets LP/MILP. Follow a rule through parameters, description, formulation, code and execution. More rules require more component calls. Defaults use temperature 1.0 and at most three execution/debug attempts. Component checks and debugging proceed automatically. title: Chain-of-Experts
description: A conductor selects experts in sequence before a reducer produces the model.
text: Chain-of-Experts (CoE) asks a conductor to select experts in sequence. Later experts read earlier comments; a reducer produces the final model and code. Each comment enters the pool available to later roles. How comments affect the next step The conductor chooses among seven expert roles. Each expert sees the problem and the current comment pool, so later comments can extend or correct earlier ones. The default selects three experts per trial before reduction. Each expert uses its role prompt and current comment pool with the run's selected LLM preset. Workflow and collaboration example Workflow overview · Choose an example stage to inspect its inputs and outputs.Download SVGFOLLOW THE EXAMPLE←Play→ 1. Interpret2. Add modeling detail3. Reduce4. Read the default path1. InterpretThis example follows useful comments into the pool, beginning with business terminology. Illustrative comment: unit profit differs from revenue; processing hours per unit differ from total hours. 2. Add modeling detailA later expert reads existing comments and adds domains, indices or resource constraints. Illustrative comment: use nonnegative integers for whole products. Cutting: 2A+B≤8; finishing: A+2B≤8. 3. ReduceThe reducer must turn comments into one internally consistent model. Conflicting comments still require an explicit final choice. Combined model: nonnegative integer quantities, total profit and two resource constraints. Follow each expert comment to its final expression. 4. Read the default pathThe default completes three expert contributions and reduction, then passes the model to the platform for solving. Default: three experts → reduction → platform solve Reflection is a deployment-preset branch. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. What reflection actually means When enabled, reflection is triggered by execution failure. Experts are questioned backwards from the latest speaker; the first accepting responsibility refines its comment. Each new trial starts with a fresh comment pool. enable_reflection=false is the default. max_trials=3 matters when reflection is enabled. Execution checks use whether the code obtains a solver status. Reading and comparing runs Look for new information: a missing rule, resolved ambiguity, domain issue or objective correction. The final model shows how comments became expressions used in computation. Use CoE for LP/MILP collaboration workflows and method comparisons. For explicit per-constraint checks see SAC-Opt; for problem-type retrieval see OptiTree. title: OptiTree
description: Match a problem type in a tree, retrieve guidance and generate code.
text: OptiTree searches a hierarchy of problem types before generating code. It makes “recognize the structure, then borrow a relevant modeling pattern” an explicit part of the workflow. What the type tree provides Transportation, assignment and staffing descriptions can share variable and constraint structures. The tree supplies modeling templates. The generator combines a template with the current costs, indices, capacities and special rules. Matching starts at the Mixed Integer Programming root and selects only among the current node's children. The deepest matched node's full entry becomes context for generation. The process retains the matching path and retrieved entry. Workflow and retrieval example Workflow overview · Choose an example stage to inspect its inputs and outputs.Download SVGFOLLOW THE EXAMPLE←Play→ 1. Recognize structure2. Use the template3. Generate and execute4. Handle no match1. Recognize structureFor warehouse-to-store transport, recognize quantities, supply and demand. The actual matching path depends on the bundled tree and LLM decisions. Decisions: shipment quantities from warehouses to stores. Inputs: unit costs, warehouse supply, store demand. 2. Use the templateA template can suggest indexed x[i,j], but the current wording determines whether supply and demand require equality or inequality. x[i,j] ≥ 0 Warehouse: sum_j x[i,j] ≤ supply[i] Store: sum_i x[i,j] ≥ demand[j], if required by the problem 3. Generate and executeUse the retrieved entry to choose a structure, then bind its indices and coefficients to the current data. Check warehouse/store indices and cost-matrix orientation. Special business rules still need explicit constraints. 4. Handle no matchUse the deepest valid entry when matching ends. An execution failure then routes code to the inspector for repair. Unknown type / missing judgment / repeated path → stop descent At most 4 code inspections. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. Why a broader match can be useful A specific but wrong type can impose the wrong structure. Treating divisible transport as one-to-one assignment can invent a restriction against split shipments. A broader match supplies general guidance while leaving details to the problem. Read the path, retrieved entry and final formulation together. The process shows the path and entry; the final model shows selected variables and constraints. Scope and related methods The current workflow targets LP/MILP, uses temperature 0 and permits four code inspections. Use it to study the effect of type retrieval. For component construction see OptiMUS; for searching multiple complete candidates see AutoFormulation. title: OR-LLM-Agent
description: Build the formulation first, then generate, execute and recheck code.
text: OR-LLM-Agent builds a formulation before generating and executing code. Its main round, infeasibility check and recheck have separate budgets, allowing execution feedback to inform later modeling decisions. Why separate formulation and code A separate formulation gives readers a checkpoint without having to recover business meaning from Python. When execution fails, inspect whether code deviates from the formulation or the formulation itself needs revision. In transport, establish warehouse supply limits, store demand and the cost objective first. A transposed cost matrix is an implementation issue; reversed demand inequalities require formulation review. Workflow and feedback example Workflow overview · Choose an example stage to inspect its inputs and outputs.Download SVGFOLLOW THE EXAMPLE←Play→ 1. State the rules2. Locate runtime errors3. Interpret the result4. Check code versions1. State the rulesCheck supply and demand directions. Whether excess delivery is permitted must come from the problem. sum_j x[i,j] ≤ supply[i] sum_i x[i,j] ≥ demand[j] min sum_i,j cost[i,j] × x[i,j] 2. Locate runtime errorsIf cost[j][i] causes an index error, use the data orientation in execution feedback to repair indexing. Hypothetical error: costs indexed store-first. Actual data: warehouse rows, store columns. 3. Interpret the resultSupply below hard demand can be genuinely infeasible. Distinguish a data conflict from a modeling error. Total supply 10, required demand 12 → shortfall 2. Review the supply limits, demand constraints and attached quantities. 4. Check code versionsUpstream round behavior can leave the final proposed repair unexecuted. Numerical results must stay attached to executed code. Intermediate artifact: latest repair proposal Numerical result: last actually executed model Run steps identify which code versions were executed. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. Separate attempt budgets The preset assigns main 3, infeasibility 1 and recheck 2 attempts. Repairs use copied conversations; only the final code returns to the main conversation. Read each round together with its actual execution record. Difference from Chat Agent “Agent” here names a fixed modeling method. Chat Agent is the user-facing optimization conversation. It can call Direct, TriVAL or other methods and handles explanations, plan selection and scenarios. You can request OR-LLM-Agent as the modeling method within Optimization chat. When to use it and what to inspect The method targets LP/MILP. Use it to inspect an explicit formulation followed by execution repair and rechecking. Locate the last actual execution first; inspect its code, status, objective and variables before reading later repair suggestions. title: ORThought
description: Write a reasoning path, formulation and code, then debug execution errors.
text: ORThought asks the LLM to state a modeling path in an expert-like order, then provide the formulation and code. The path is retained so readers can understand why variables, objectives and constraints were chosen. What a useful modeling path explains Useful explanations name concrete choices: “whole products require integer quantities” or “processing hours add across products, so capacity is consumption times quantity.” The path links each business rule to its variable domain or mathematical expression. The current workflow uses the upstream formalized mode and outputs a modeling path, formulation and code. The process view retains this explanation as a separate solution_path artifact. Check execution4. Read back results1. Identify decisionsSeparate production decisions from known inputs. Decide production quantities A and B. Profit, processing times and capacity are given parameters. 2. Explain expressionsConnect each expression to its business meaning instead of listing unexplained formulae. Whole units → nonnegative integer A, B Additive hours → 2A+B≤8, A+2B≤8 Total profit → max 3A+2B 3. Check executionIf code cannot obtain a solver status, debugging reads the problem, formulation, code and actual error. title: LLMOPT
description: Construct a five-part formulation and route corrections to the affected stage.
text: LLMOPT connects language and code through a five-part formulation: Sets, Parameters, Variables, Objective and Constraints. After execution, self-correction judges the formulation and code separately and returns to the affected stage. How five elements locate errors The structure separates objects, known quantities, decisions, goals and requirements. Indices, units and domains have explicit places, making it easier to distinguish a modeling error from an implementation error. Element Production example Sets Products P={A,B}; resources R={cutting,finishing} Parameters Profit p, consumption matrix a, capacity b Variables Nonnegative integer quantities x[p] Objective Maximize total profit Constraints Resource use cannot exceed each capacity Workflow and correction example Workflow overview · Choose an example stage to inspect its inputs and outputs.Download SVGFOLLOW THE EXAMPLE←Play→ 1. State structure2. Translate to code3. Choose the return point4. Read final evidence1. State structurePreserve whole-unit requirements, resource dimensions and parameter values. Translate to codeBuild the native model from the five elements, then execute. Check corresponding variables, objective and resource constraints. If only code uses the wrong domain, regenerate code alone. Wrong formulation → Q2F → F2C → solve Only code wrong → F2C → solve 4. Read final evidenceUse the last execution for numerical evidence. The run retains correction judgments alongside execution status. Up to 12 re-solves after the first execution. Final result uses the last actual execution. title: AutoFormulation
description: Search candidate components and rank complete models with MCTS and comparisons.
text: AutoFormulation searches a tree of modeling components. It checks, deduplicates and ranks candidates, explores complete models with Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS), then selects a solved candidate through pairwise ranking. What is being searched Tree levels are parameters, decision variables, objective, equality constraints and inequality constraints. A root-to-leaf path is a complete model. Integer versus continuous production quantities, for example, are different variable choices affecting all later components. Each candidate path has its own formulation, code and execution record. Pairwise judgments compare how well the candidate models express the original problem, and the resulting ranking guides further search. Construction, search and ranking Workflow overview · Choose an example stage to inspect its inputs and outputs.Download SVGFOLLOW THE EXAMPLE←Play→ 1. Build candidates2. Select a path3. Establish comparisons4. Select final model1. Build candidatesEquivalent notation should be deduplicated, while invalid components need checking. Equivalent expressions are grouped before the candidate tree is expanded. Candidate 1: nonnegative integer A, B Candidate 2: nonnegative integer x[p], p∈{A,B} These may differ only in notation. 2. Select a pathUCT balances promising and underexplored paths. A complete path must be assembled and solved before becoming a solved candidate. Parameters → variables → objective → equalities → inequalities Each complete candidate has its own code and execution result. 3. Establish comparisonsThe first 3 solved models become baselines with reward 0.5. Later candidates are compared against baselines in both orders. Compare each candidate with baselines in both orders. Return comparison win rates as search rewards. 4. Select final modelBradley–Terry ranking selects the final solved model. Rankings are model judgments; readers still inspect domains and rules. Output: selected formulation, code and actual solver result. The process retains candidate paths, rankings and execution artifacts. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. Equivalence and reward Parameters use a mode, variable candidates use repeated LLM grouping, and other expressions use symbolic SymPy/Z3 scripts for equivalence. Generated checking scripts run in the sandbox. UCT uses exploration weight w_exp=1 and node-reward weight lambda_cte=0.5. Repeated judgments in both comparison orders reduce dependence on a single reply or order. These judgments produce relative candidate preferences. Why the budget is much larger Defaults sample 8 completions per node, retain 3 candidates, use 5 ranking completions and run 16 rollouts. Initial tree construction can need about 540 completions; a later comparison can need about 30. Pruning reduces actual use. Its default run limits reach 20,000 LLM calls, 1,000 solves and 6 hours. Check deployment limits first. Administrators adjust the sampling and search budgets in deployment presets. When it is useful Use it for LP/MILP candidate-modeling and search research, especially when inspecting structural alternatives. Explicit units, indices and field meanings reduce unhelpful candidates. For one inspectable first model with a smaller call budget, start with Direct or Feedback Repair. Source and platform adaptation Based on the pinned AutoFormulator implementation and ICML 2025 paper. The platform retains construction, MCTS and ranking, supplies sandboxed native-library code, bounds unparseable-comparison retries and fixes the reversed two-candidate comparison direction. title: SAC-Opt
description: Extract semantic anchors and selectively repair constraints after backtranslation.
text: SAC-Opt preserves business meaning as semantic anchors, translates constraint code back into language, and compares that translation with the anchors. Failed constraints are repaired selectively; accepted components are frozen. Why read code backwards “Each employee works at most five days” requires summing over dates. Summing over employees can instead mean “at most five employees per day.” Both programs may execute while expressing different rules. The backtranslator reads constraint code and context to state its expressed rule. A comparator checks that translation against the original semantic anchor and returns a pass or repair decision. Workflow and constraint-level example Workflow overview · Choose an example stage to inspect its inputs and outputs.Download SVGFOLLOW THE EXAMPLE←Play→ 1. Keep anchors2. Backtranslate3. Selective repair4. Assemble and run1. Keep anchorsDefine binary x[e,d] for employee e and date d. Preserve requirements with their quantifiers and index meanings. x[e,d] = 1 if employee e works on date d. C1: each employee works at most 5 days. C2: at least 3 employees each day. 2. BacktranslateSuppose C1 mistakenly sums over employees. The translation reveals that it actually limits daily headcount. Hypothetical error: for each d, sum(x[e,d] for e in E) ≤ 5 Translation: at most 5 employees each day. 3. Selective repairRepair C1's quantifier and summation direction. Freeze C2 if it passed, avoiding unrelated rewrites. Repair C1: for each e, sum(x[e,d] for d in D) ≤ 5 Freeze C2: for each d, sum(x[e,d] for e in E) ≥ 3 4. Assemble and runAssemble checked components and execute the complete model. Preserve an explicit unresolved status if semantic checks exhaust their budget. Semantic consistency: recorded per constraint Executability: checked on the complete program Numerical plan: returned by the actual backend Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. From four anchor types to code Parameter and variable anchors capture symbols, shapes, units, domains and bounds. The current implementation retains parameters and variables with confidence scores above 3; low-confidence constraints receive further assessment. Code is generated as setup, objective and individual constraints, with component counts checked against anchors. Full attachments remain accessible through build_model(data). Components can be submitted in batches; each constraint receives its own consistency decision. Limits and failure interpretation Defaults allow five parse attempts, five semantic rounds and three full-program executions. Semantic checking and execution debugging are separate loops: one checks meaning, the other handles runtime failures. The final record retains unresolved constraint checks, their feedback and the solver result. Open a failed check to inspect its anchor, backtranslation and associated code. When to consider this workflow Use it for LP/MILP problems with many rules, fragile indices or quantifiers, and a need to inspect individual constraints. Compared with TriVAL, its focus is anchor-to-constraint-code consistency. Compared with Feedback Repair, repair is more granular. Platform implementation and sources This is an independent implementation of the published algorithm, using prompts written by this project. The pinned reference is Forrest-Stone/SAC-Opt. The platform retains anchors, blind backtranslation and selective repair, with batched components and native-model contracts. The published source records the component and contract adaptations. title: BIND
description: Show data structure to the LLM and read complete attachments during execution.
text: BIND separates understanding data structure from reading complete values. The LLM sees fields, types and sizes; generated code reads the full JSON/CSV during execution. This addresses truncated previews, long-table transcription and data-binding errors. Why structure can be enough Model structure often does not depend on every individual value. A transport model needs to know that costs form a warehouse-by-store matrix and demand is indexed by store. It need not copy every matrix entry into a prompt and back into code. Describe field meanings in the problem: for example, whether capacity measures hours or units, and which objects index each matrix row and column. Choose nonnegative integer quantities to maximize total profit without exceeding any resource.” The correct result is A=3, B=2, objective 13. title: OptiMind
description: Combine public problem-type hints with multi-turn solver feedback.
text: OptiMind combines public problem-type hints with multi-turn solver feedback. A successful solve still produces feedback, allowing another revision or a final textual answer that ends the trajectory. What the hint library provides Type hints highlight common modeling mistakes. In traveling salesperson models, one incoming and one outgoing edge per city can still produce separate subtours; additional constraints must enforce a single tour. The public library currently contains only TravelingSalesman, with six error/hint pairs. Classification selects a public type or no match. Unmatched problems receive general checking guidance. Workflow and checking example Workflow overview · Choose an example stage to inspect its inputs and outputs.Download SVGFOLLOW THE EXAMPLE←Play→ 1. Match hints2. Generate and solve3. Check success too4. End one trajectory1. Match hintsTraveling salesperson problems can use public specialist hints. Other types use general checks when no public entry matches. Example: visit every city once and return to the start. Reminder: in-degree/out-degree constraints do not eliminate separate subtours. 2. Generate and solveThe generator turns hints into constraints; the process retains both the hint and generated formulation. Inspect binary edges, degree constraints and subtour elimination. Actual solver execution provides the numerical result. 3. Check success tooRead selected edges even after optimality. Separate cycles identify a connectivity rule to inspect. Two disjoint cycles → inspect connectivity constraints. Faithful model and result → final answer can end the run. 4. End one trajectoryThe default follows one generation-and-feedback trajectory. A final answer ends the run and retains the last executed model. At most 5 generations; temperature 0.6; top_p 0.95. Final artifacts include the executed code, status and values. Worked example: illustrative inputs and intermediate artifacts. Revision and stopping Feedback includes successful as well as failed statuses, objectives and values. Revised code continues the generate–execute–feedback loop. After a valid execution, a final reply without code can stop it. Without any valid execution, a code-free reply is not completion; code is requested again within the budget. Final numbers come from the last executed model. Comparing related workflows Feedback Repair has an explicit accept-or-repair review. OptiMind centers on hints and continuing feedback within one trajectory. OptiTree retrieves entries from a hierarchical type tree, a different source and use of guidance. Use it to inspect the effect of public hints. Choose a library and backend for the model structure; the type-specific hints apply to the matched problem family. Weights, orchestration and specialist hints are separate experimental conditions. The platform preserves public hint files, adds optional type matching and supplies native-model contracts and actual solver feedback. The public hint files and adaptation are available in source. title: Pyomo
description: Express algebraic models and connect compatible native backends.
text: Pyomo expresses optimization in a form close to mathematical notation. Products, factories and dates become index sets; objectives and constraints use those indices, making business rules easier to map to code. Start with the mathematics Choose whole-unit quantities A and B, maximize 3A+2B, and enforce cutting 2A+B≤8 and finishing A+2B≤8. The integer optimum is A=3, B=2, objective 13. If quantities are genuinely divisible, continuous domains give A=B=8/3 and objective 40/3. The selected domain is recorded in the model. Complete platform code import pyomo.environ as pyo def build_model(data): model = pyo.ConcreteModel() model.products = pyo.Set(initialize=["A", "B"]) profit = {"A": 3, "B": 2} model.x = pyo.Var(model.products, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers) model.profit = pyo.Objective( expr=sum(profit[p] * model.x[p] for p in model.products), sense=pyo.maximize, ) model.cutting = pyo.Constraint(expr=2*model.x["A"] + model.x["B"] <= 8) model.finishing = pyo.Constraint(expr=model.x["A"] + 2*model.x["B"] <= 8) return model Return the built model; the platform selects a backend, solves and reads named variables. For attachments, parse complete parameters with json.loads(data['production.json']); see BIND. From expressions to solving Workflow overviewDownload SVG Pyomo connects compatible engines through native adapters. The platform accepts ConcreteModel, instantiated AbstractModel and Kernel. Algebraic models normally default to HiGHS; Kernel defaults to compatible CBC. Common expression mistakes Use binary variables or suitable logical formulations for decisions that activate constraints. Use native Pyomo expressions for relationships among unknown variables. Inspect index sets in indexed constraints. Use pyo.Constraint.Skip when an index should be omitted. Instantiate AbstractModel before returning it. Checking results Read x[A] and x[B], substitute them into both resources, and recompute profit with units. Confirm the actual backend and integer domain. Execution feedback identifies backend compatibility issues. Try it: change capacity and minimum ordersINTERACTIVEA earns CNY 3 per unit and B earns CNY 2. title: gurobipy / Gurobi
description: Use Gurobi's native Python models, matrix API and conflict evidence.
text: gurobipy constructs native Gurobi models. It suits workflows using native variables, constraints, matrix expressions and diagnostics. Scalar and matrix APIs both construct gp.Model and can be chosen to match data structure. Production, transportation and location LP/MILP are common starting points. Complete production model import gurobipy as gp from gurobipy import GRB def build_model(data): model = gp.Model("production") a = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="A") b = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="B") model.setObjective(3*a + 2*b, GRB.MAXIMIZE) model.addConstr(2*a + b <= 8, name="cutting") model.addConstr(a + 2*b <= 8, name="finishing") return model Return the built model for platform execution: A=3, B=2 and profit CNY 13. Supported linear Gurobi paths can produce an IIS identifying jointly inconsistent constraints or bounds. An IIS lists an irreducible set of conflicting constraints or bounds to help locate requirements for revision. Named constraints improve the connection to requirements; see infeasibility and conflicts. title: OR-Tools
description: Use native linear, integer, constraint, routing and network-flow interfaces.
text: OR-Tools provides mathematical programming, constraint programming, routing and graph algorithms. The platform recognizes the returned native model and uses its corresponding solving path. Choose the native interface by task Interface Model structure Backend examples MPSolver / MathOpt / ModelBuilder Linear, integer and interface-supported mathematical programming Compatible SCIP, HIGHS and other engines CpModel / CP-SAT Finite integers, Booleans, scheduling and logic CP_SAT RoutingModel Vehicles, visits, capacities and time windows ROUTING Original Constraint Solver Finite-domain constraints and search CP Maximum / minimum-cost flow Network arcs, capacities, costs and supply MAX_FLOW, MIN_COST_FLOW Assignment / knapsack One-to-one matching and capacity-limited selection ASSIGNMENT, KNAPSACK_* Select OR-Tools and a backend in settings; code determines the API. The default mathematical-programming reference uses SCIP. HIGHS can use MathOpt. A complete CP-SAT staffing model Four employees each work one day. Monday and Tuesday each need two employees. x[e,d] indicates whether employee e works on day d; costs are in the matrix below. from ortools.sat.python import cp_model def build_model(data): costs = [[1, 7], [2, 8], [7, 1], [8, 2]] model = cp_model.CpModel() x = {(e, d): model.new_bool_var(f"work[{e},{d}]") for e in range(4) for d in range(2)} for e in range(4): model.add(sum(x[e, d] for d in range(2)) == 1) for d in range(2): model.add(sum(x[e, d] for e in range(4)) == 2) model.minimize(sum(costs[e][d] * x[e, d] for e in range(4) for d in range(2))) return model Choose CP_SAT. Employees 0 and 1 work Monday; 2 and 3 work Tuesday, for cost 6. Requiring employee 0 on Tuesday raises the optimum to 18. Use scenario comparison for independent staffing changes. CP-SAT model structure Workflow overviewDownload SVG Integer domains, logic and interval variables express discrete schedules. Fractional durations can be represented in a consistent integer unit, such as minutes. Use that unit throughout inputs and convert results for presentation. Minimum-cost flow normally returns its native model. The original Constraint Solver returns the model and variables, plus objective and sense for optimization. See the native-interface reference. Reading and using results Named CP-SAT Boolean variables map directly to employees and days. Read Routing output as visit sequences together with objective, status and route requirements. Export full variables or use plan conversation to query an employee and calculate daily totals. See the official CP-SAT guide, Routing guide and MathOpt documentation.

title: CPMpy
description: Model discrete decisions with integer, Boolean and global constraints.
text: CPMpy expresses discrete decisions with finite-domain integers, Booleans and global constraints. Arrays fit employees, dates, machines and tasks; AllDifferent, Element and Cumulative express common rules directly. How global constraints simplify a model Three vehicles each serve one of three stores, with exactly one vehicle per store. Let destination[i] identify vehicle i's store. AllDifferent(destination) expresses distinct destinations; costs are indexed from each vehicle's cost row. Each variable has domain 0 through 2, with each value identifying a store. CPMpy passes these finite-domain expressions to a native backend. Complete assignment model import cpmpy as cp def build_model(data): cost = cp.cpm_array([[4, 8, 6], [7, 3, 9], [5, 6, 2]]) destination = cp.intvar(0, 2, shape=3, name="destination") model = cp.Model(cp.AllDifferent(destination)) model.minimize(sum(cost[i, destination[i]] for i in range(3))) return model The default backend is OR-Tools CP-SAT. The optimum assigns vehicles 0, 1 and 2 to stores 0, 1 and 2, for 4+3+2=9. Adding destination[1] != 1 raises the optimum to 17. Expressions, compilation and solving Workflow overviewDownload SVG The platform accepts cp.Model and native SolverInterface. Backends come from SolverLookup and installed subsolvers. ortools is the default; run settings show the available alternatives. Common rule patterns Business rule Expression pattern Tasks use different machines AllDifferent Selected index determines a cost Variable array indexing / Element expressions A requires B a.implies(b) Tasks share limited capacity Cumulative Find any assignment satisfying rules Model without an objective Integer variables have finite bounds; Booleans represent selections. Consistent integer units keep quantities and logical relationships clear. Conflict analysis and results The platform's CPMpy path supports MUS conflict evidence, connecting inconsistent constraints to requirements. Clear names and indices help in infeasibility analysis. Interpret destination[0] using the store-number mapping in the formulation. Export complete values, query a vehicle in plan conversation, or revise available destinations. Selection and references Start here for finite domains, logic, exclusions and global constraints. See Pyomo for continuous quantities and OR-Tools for Routing. The official CPMpy solver guide describes native interfaces and backends.

title: PuLP
description: Build linear and mixed-integer models with CBC or other native backends.
text: PuLP targets linear and mixed-integer programming. Variables, linear sums and inequalities suit production, transportation, budgets and allocation when relationships are linear. What linear means 3A+2B and 2A+B≤8 are linear because coefficients are known constants. A×B, A² and division by an unknown variable are not. Convex quadratic losses and norms can use libraries such as CVXPY, linked below. Binary decisions can still express switches in a linear model. With a valid capacity bound, production ≤ capacity × open links production to a binary opening decision because capacity is constant. Complete production model import pulp def build_model(data): model = pulp.LpProblem("production", pulp.LpMaximize) a = pulp.LpVariable("A", lowBound=0, cat="Integer") b = pulp.LpVariable("B", lowBound=0, cat="Integer") model += 3*a + 2*b, "profit" model += 2*a + b <= 8, "cutting" model += a + 2*b <= 8, "finishing" return model The expression without a comparison defines the objective; comparison expressions add constraints. Names must be unique. The platform calls CBC or the explicit compatible backend; generated code does not call model.solve(). Default backend and interfaces The default is PULP_CBC_CMD. Other backends are discovered through native listSolvers/getSolver, preserving Python, command-line and dynamic-library identifiers. Row-oriented algebra and column-oriented LpConstraintVar both return LpProblem. Choose a form matching the data organization. Review and revise results The example gives A=3, B=2 and objective 13. Results show variables, objective and actual backend. Export the full data or revise capacities and minimum demand from the saved plan. Try it: change capacity and minimum ordersINTERACTIVEA earns CNY 3 per unit and B earns CNY 2. Change available hours and minimum orders to compare quantities and total profit. Cutting hours 8 Minimum B0345 Quantity typeInteger: whole unitsContinuous: divisible units Maximize 3A + 2B2A + B ≤ 8；A + 2B ≤ 8；B ≥ 0A and B are nonnegative integers Cutting limitFinishing limitFeasible regionBest planA = 3, B = 2 · Profit CNY 13 Cutting: 8 / 8 hours. Finishing: 7 / 8 hours. Download plan CSVResetA fixed teaching example, computed instantly in your browser. Enable JavaScript to change this example. The initial values and explanation remain above. Change cutting capacity or minimum B in the example and download the current CSV. See revisions and scenario comparison for the platform workflow. Common issues and selection Specify cat="Integer" for whole quantities and cat="Binary" for switches. Inspect names, objective direction and every resource constraint. For variable-product expressions, select a library supporting the required structure. See Pyomo for broader algebraic modeling, CVXPY for convex norms and quadratic losses, or CPMpy for discrete logic and global constraints. API details are in the official PuLP documentation.

title: CVXPY
description: Model convex optimization and select a backend for its cones and domains.
text: CVXPY builds convex and related models with structured mathematical expressions. Native atoms for squared losses, norms, linear maps and cones suit fitting, allocation, portfolio weights and regularized optimization. A complete convex quadratic example Choose continuous (x,y) near target (1,2), with nonnegative quantities and a total resource limit of 2: min⁡x,y≥0(x−1)2+(y−2)2s.t.x+y≤2.\min_{x,y\ge0}(x-1)^2+(y-2)^2\quad\text{s.t.}\quad x+y\le2.minx,y≥0​(x−1)2+(y−2)2s.t.x+y≤2. The optimum is (0.5,1.5), objective 0.5. import cvxpy as cp def build_model(data): x = cp.Variable(2, nonneg=True, name="allocation") objective = cp.Minimize(cp.sum_squares(x - [1.0, 2.0])) return cp.Problem(objective, [cp.sum(x) <= 2]) Select CVXPY. OSQP supports this continuous convex quadratic objective with linear constraints. Return Problem; the platform solves and reads its variable array. Explore resource changes Try convex optimization: the nearest feasible pointINTERACTIVEMinimize (x − 1)² + (y − 2)²x + y ≤ 2；x, y ≥ 0 Total resource limit 2 Feasible regionTarget (1, 2)Optimumx = 0.5, y = 1.5 · 0.5 The optimum is the feasible point nearest to (1, 2). The objective is the squared distance. A fixed teaching example, computed instantly in your browser. Enable JavaScript to change this example. The initial values and explanation remain above. Increase the limit from 2 to 3 to move the solution toward the target. A line connects target and solution; the ellipse is an equal-objective contour around the target. Variable components map to x and y in array order. From expressions to a backend Workflow overviewDownload SVG DCP describes disciplined convex expressions; DGP uses positive variables and geometric-programming structure; DQCP handles recognized quasiconvex structure. The platform detects the mode, using gp=True for DGP and qcp=True for DQCP. Select a backend Model Typical backend direction Continuous convex quadratic objective, linear constraints OSQP Supported continuous cones Clarabel, SCS and others Integer or Boolean decisions A mixed-integer backend supporting the model structure Native MOSEK capabilities MOSEK with configured license AUTO uses a compatible installed solver_path and records the actual engine. Explicit selection fixes the computation path. See backends for installation and licenses. Expressions and further use Use @ for matrix multiplication, cp.sum, cp.norm and cp.quad_form for the corresponding expressions. Nonnegative, positive and integer variable attributes help structure recognition. Map business switches and selections to the appropriate domains. After reviewing complete values, use plan conversation for derived totals or revised budgets. See official documentation for solvers, DGP and DQCP.

title: PySCIPOpt / SCIP
description: Use native SCIP for linear, integer and nonlinear constraints.
text: PySCIPOpt uses native SCIP models for linear, integer and nonlinear constraints. It suits models combining discrete choices with native nonlinear expressions. Expressing a nonlinear objective The native interface uses a linear objective. Introduce auxiliary t, constrain cost(x)≤t, and minimize t. This epigraph form preserves the cost while fitting the interface. The example minimizes squared distance to (1,2) under a resource limit of 2. Auxiliary loss represents that cost. Complete native model from pyscipopt import Model def build_model(data): model = Model("allocation") x = model.addVar(name="x", lb=0, vtype="C") y = model.addVar(name="y", lb=0, vtype="C") loss = model.addVar(name="loss", lb=0, vtype="C") model.addCons(x + y <= 2, name="resource") model.addCons((x-1)**2 + (y-2)**2 <= loss, name="loss_definition") model.setObjective(loss, "minimize") return model SCIP should return values near x=0.5, y=1.5 and loss=0.5, read with numerical tolerances. Return Model; the platform performs solving. How the auxiliary variable works Workflow overviewDownload SVG For maximization, the corresponding hypograph uses t≤reward(x) and maximizes t. Objective direction determines the linking inequality. Meaningful names help explain auxiliary values. Variables, indices and matrices vtype="C" means continuous, "I" integer and "B" binary. Scalar and matrix APIs return pyscipopt.Model. Parse full attachments to construct indexed products, times or network decisions. For mixed discrete/nonlinear models, choose a modeling method covering that mathematics. Runs retain the library, backend and method together. Results and further operations Auxiliary variables are part of the saved model. Export all values and explain which variables are business decisions versus cost or logical auxiliaries. Use revisions to change resources or fix discrete choices and compare plans. See CVXPY for geometry and an interactive version of the continuous example. Native APIs are documented in PySCIPOpt Model and the matrix tutorial.

title: CasADi
description: Express smooth nonlinear models and understand plugin and local-solution semantics.
text: CasADi builds optimization problems with symbolic expressions and automatic differentiation. Opti organizes variables, objectives and constraints; Ipopt is a common path for smooth continuous nonlinear models. A complete nonlinear model This single-variable objective has two wells, allowing exploration of starting points and local results: min⁡−2≤x≤2 (x2−1)2+0.2x.\min_{-2\le x\le2}\;(x^2-1)^2+0.2x.min−2≤x≤2​(x2−1)2+0.2x. import casadi as ca def build_model(data): model = ca.Opti() x = model.variable() model.minimize((x*x - 1)**2 + 0.2*x) model.subject_to(model.bounded(-2, x, 2)) model.set_initial(x, -1.8) return model Select CasADi and Ipopt. Initial values, bounds and smooth expressions enter the solve. Results use native CasADi variable names; describe component meanings in the formulation. Play a local-search illustration Try local optimization: why the starting point mattersINTERACTIVEf(x) = (x² − 1)² + 0.2xGradient descent step size = 0.04 Starting point−1.80.31.8 Play iterationsResetIteration 0 · x = −1.8 · f(x) = 4.658 Choose a start and play 60 gradient steps. The green trail shows which minimum the iterations approach. A fixed teaching example, computed instantly in your browser. Enable JavaScript to change this example. The initial values and explanation remain above. This interaction uses fixed-step gradient descent to display iterations on the function. Choose a starting point and inspect the path, iteration count and objective. Platform CasADi runs use the selected native plugin. Solving symbolic problems Workflow overviewDownload SVG Opti NLP commonly uses Ipopt. Opti Conic can specify a compatible plugin such as qrqp. Integer domains use set_domain with a compatible plugin such as Bonmin. Available plugins come from the execution environment's native registry. Maximization and low-level interfaces For maximizing f, minimize -f and return the objective sign so reported values use the original objective: return {"model": model, "objective_sign": -1} Low-level nlpsol/qpsol/conic returns provide problem, arguments, optional solver and options. Native decision vectors are recorded as x[i], supporting explicit numerical arguments, sparse structure and plugin configuration. Using results and continuing Nonconvex NLP results retain local status. Run different starts, bounds or requirements as separate scenarios and compare actual values and objectives with saved configurations. CasADi suits smooth nonlinear continuous, control and trajectory models. See CVXPY for convex quadratic/conic structure and OR-Tools for combinatorial tasks. Refer to the CasADi documentation and plugin API.

title: coptpy / COPT
description: Use the native COPT interface and check model and license requirements.
text: coptpy constructs native COPT models for LP, MILP, convex quadratic and supported conic optimization. Scalar and matrix APIs use the COPT engine. When native interfaces help Use it when a team already works with COPT and wants consistent native models and execution. For indexed production models, use addVars to name quantities by product, then sum profits and resource use over that index. Matrix interfaces express the same coefficients as arrays. Complete production model import coptpy as cp from coptpy import COPT def build_model(data): model = cp.Envr().createModel("production") a = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=COPT.INTEGER, name="A") b = model.addVar(lb=0, vtype=COPT.INTEGER, name="B") model.setObjective(3*a + 2*b, COPT.MAXIMIZE) model.addConstr(2*a + b <= 8, name="cutting") model.addConstr(a + 2*b <= 8, name="finishing") return model Return the model; the platform solves it. The integer optimum is A=3, B=2, objective 13. Indexed models can use addVars; matrix APIs still require correct dimensions. Convex quadratic structure and integer domains Validate a small linear case first. Adding quadratic costs requires checking convexity and backend support. Integer decisions also require the appropriate mixed-integer capability. Try it: change capacity and minimum ordersINTERACTIVEA earns CNY 3 per unit and B earns CNY 2. Change available hours and minimum orders to compare quantities and total profit. Cutting hours 8 Minimum B0345 Quantity typeInteger: whole unitsContinuous: divisible units Maximize 3A + 2B2A + B ≤ 8；A + 2B ≤ 8；B ≥ 0A and B are nonnegative integers Cutting limitFinishing limitFeasible regionBest planA = 3, B = 2 · Profit CNY 13 Cutting: 8 / 8 hours. Finishing: 7 / 8 hours. Download plan CSVResetA fixed teaching example, computed instantly in your browser. Enable JavaScript to change this example. The initial values and explanation remain above. Changing the quantity domain changes the example's mathematics. The interaction shows the corresponding values and objective. Licensing and deployment Follow the COPT installation guide to obtain a license matching the installed major version. It provides license.dat and license.key for deployment. Deployment uses COPT_LICENSE_DIR with the specific license.dat and license.key files mounted read-only for the sandbox. Package installation, library loading and license validation are separate steps; see backends and licenses. Checking results and references Inspect engine, status, objective direction and decision values. Distinguish a retained feasible incumbent from proven optimality after a limit. Use hand calculations for small resource models and retain full models and exports for larger reviews. See the COPT Python documentation and installation and licensing guide.

Errors identify interface, dependency or license issues. After installation or updates Compose builds backend dependencies into the Worker. Python setups use uv run llm4om build-worker.
